verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days" (R1); "10-day journey" (R2); "Scheduled for almost 10 days" (R3); "approximately 10 days" (R5); "The 10-day Artemis II mission ... test flight" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm ~10-day duration and describe it as a crewed test flight of systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago" (R1, 2026-53≈1973, Apollo 17=1972); "53 years after Apollo 17" (R5); "first time in over 50 years" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is designed to validate the Orion spacecraft's systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "thoroughly test their Orion capsule" (R1); "test flights for ... Orion" (R3); "flight test Orion’s life-support systems" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for testing/validating Orion systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is launching April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT" on April 1, 2026 (R1); "as early as April 1" (R3); "targeting Wednesday, April 1, 2026" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew includes Wiseman, Glover, Koch, and Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R1); same names (R2, R3, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal is to test the Orion capsule, its life support systems, and the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket with humans on board.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test their Orion capsule ... life support systems" ... "SLS rocket" (R1); "test ... SLS and Orion ... with crew" (R3, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to mission goals of testing Orion, life support, and SLS with crew.

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis I ... uncrewed" (R3); "second SLS launch ... uncrewed ... Artemis I" (R5); "follow-up mission to the uncrewed Artemis I" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II follows successful uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Reid Wiseman ... Victor Glover ... Christina Koch ... Canadian Space Agency’s Jeremy Hansen" (multiple, exact phrasing in R8)
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew composition and affiliations stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II flight path takes the crew behind the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "loop around it, getting ... view of the far side of the moon" (R1); "beyond the moon’s far side" (R2); "around the Moon’s far side" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of path behind far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goes further into space than any human has traveled since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "travel farther from Earth than anyone before them" ... "since ... 1972" (R1); "farther from Earth than any humans have traveled before" (R2); breaks Apollo record (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm record distance since 1972.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is expected to last roughly 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "about nine and a half days"; "10-day journey"; "almost 10 days"; "approximately 10 days"; "10-day" (multiple)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent ~10-day duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concludes with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown ... Pacific Ocean" (R1, R2); "splashes down in the Pacific Ocean" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit splashdown location.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will test manual piloting of the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Crew manually pilots Orion for the first time" (R1); "manual close-range maneuvering" (R4); "opportunity ... to pilot the spacecraft in manual mode" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mention of manual piloting tests.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will perform in-orbit inspections before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "put their Orion capsule through its paces"; "check out the Orion capsule" (R1); "23-hour checkout of the Orion spacecraft" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe systems checks/outfitting in orbit before TLI/return, but not explicitly 'inspections'; broader terms used.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch site is Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R1); "Florida's Kennedy Space Center" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Exact site confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch Complex 39B"; "Pad 39B"; lifted off April 1 (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Precise location and date.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew spends the first 24+ hours checking systems in high elliptical orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "spending about 24 hours orbiting ... highly elliptical 24-hour-long orbit ... check out" (R1); "high elliptical orbit ... 23-hour checkout" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Matches timeline, orbit type, and activity.

verifications.claim: Artemis II Trans-Lunar Injection occurs on Day 2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first 24 hours ... then ... trans-lunar injection" (R1); "Flight Day 2: ... trans-lunar injection burn" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit Day 2 TLI.

verifications.claim: Artemis II Trans-Lunar Injection sends the crew on a figure-eight free-return trajectory around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "figure eight on a free-return trajectory" (R3); "figure-eight free-return trajectory" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct trajectory description post-TLI.

verifications.claim: Artemis II Lunar Flyby occurs on Day 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 6 during the lunar flyby" (R2, launch Apr 1); "Flight Day 6: ... lunar flyby" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Confirms Day 6 flyby.

verifications.claim: During Artemis II Lunar Flyby, the crew conducts a close pass to the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "loop around ... far side" (R1); "closest approach to the Moon ... far side" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Flyby involves close pass to far side.

verifications.claim: During Artemis II Lunar Flyby, the crew photographs the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "take photos of the lunar surface during the lunar flyby" ... "far side" (R2); "take photos of the far side of the Moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit photography during flyby of far side.

verifications.claim: Artemis II splashdown occurs on Day 10 in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown on April 10" (R1, R2, launch Apr 1=Day 10); "Day 10: ... splashes down in the Pacific Ocean" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact day and location.
